Uplink channel quality and throughput indicators were moderate — UL_SNR ranged from 15.6 dB to 21.6 dB with a mean of 17.7 dB, and UL_MCS varied between 14.0 and 18.0 with a mean of 16.1. Downlink MCS remained fixed at 7, and downlink BLER stayed at 0.0. Uplink BLER showed a transient degradation, peaking at 0.25 (minimum 0.046, mean 0.12) during t=55–67.

Resource use on the uplink was variable: UL_NPRB spanned 10.4 to 29.1 (mean 18.7), while PRBs allocated on the uplink were low (0.58 to 3.3, mean 1.6) and UL PRB utilization mirrored that (0.6% to 3.4%, mean 1.6%). Downlink PRBs and utilization were substantially higher: PRBs_DL_Current ranged 61.2 to 68.4 (mean 64.4) and PRB_Utilization_DL ranged 57.8% to 74.6% (mean 65.7%).

Traffic volume was dominated by uplink bytes: TX_Bytes ranged from 388,032 Bytes to 448,843 Bytes with a mean of 417,365.1 Bytes, while RX_Bytes ranged from 3,003 Bytes to 14,056 Bytes with a mean of 5,776.3 Bytes. The estimated uplink buffer occupied between 154.9 KB and 757.9 KB with an average of 297.1 KB. Packet counts reflected bursty downlink activity: UL_NumberOfPackets ranged 35 to 130 (mean 65.8), and DL_NumberOfPackets surged to 1,355 during t=36–43 (overall range 0 to 1,355, mean 277.1).

From a protocol standpoint, uplink traffic was exclusively TCP (100%), while downlink was TCP for about 79.69% of timestamps and had no UDP usage. Overall, the session shows constrained downlink modulation, moderate uplink SNR/MCS, occasional uplink BLER spikes, concentrated DL PRB usage, and predominantly TCP transport.
